No, I don’t think I’m checking it, like “did I open it right” or “did I close it right.” The drawer is open, or it isn’t — that part’s usually obvious.

I guess… I’m not sure. I don’t really walk around thinking, “this is a habit, and it’s reasonable,” you know? It’s more like… I’m at the register and my hand just gets stuck in the wrong thing, like tapping the scanner in a pattern when I should be scanning, or I freeze over the cash drawer while someone’s waiting.\n\nAnd then the line builds up, and that makes me nervous after, because people stare. It reminds me of when the card machine used to jam all the time—everybody thinks it’s your fault, even if it isn’t. But this time it’s me doing it, I guess. Last week they wrote me up for it.\n\nDoctor: Right before you tap or freeze, do you get an unwanted thought or urge that feels like you have to act on it?\n\nPatient: It’s not like there’s a thought first, exactly. I’ve worked registers a long time, so I know how it’s supposed to go.
